about.hero.title: About DigitalHome.Cloud
about.hero.subtitle: Technology supporting nature, simplicity, and human creativity.
about.p1: DigitalHome.Cloud is an open, extensible platform designed to help people plan, build, and operate smart homes in a holistic and sustainable way. The philosophy behind the platform comes from D-LAB-5 — a mindset where technology is a supporting tool, never the main driver.
about.p2: Through a combination of semantic models, automation, and intuitive design tools, DigitalHome.Cloud aims to connect the digital and physical worlds in a way that enhances quality of life, reduces complexity, and respects nature.
about.vision.title: The Vision
about.vision.body: DigitalHome.Cloud is the beginning of a larger ecosystem where modern technology, traditional craft, and environmental awareness meet. Inspired by the spirit of “Where roots meet digital”, the platform grows organically: feature by feature, home by home, always keeping humans at the center.
about.oss.title: Open Source & Community
about.oss.body: All core components of the platform are open source under the DigitalHome-cloud GitHub organization. Community contributions, ideas, and collaborations are encouraged to help create a future where smart homes are accessible, sustainable, and user-friendly.
about.dlab.title: Powered by D-LAB-5
about.dlab.body: D-LAB-5 is a family-led innovation initiative combining engineering, sustainable architecture, design, and nature-inspired problem solving. DigitalHome.Cloud is one of the first projects built under this umbrella.

link.title: Link an edge
link.subtitle: An edge (the home's box, or an app on a computer) shows a pairing code. Approve it here and the edge is linked to your account and, if you choose, to one of your homes. No password is typed on the edge.
link.approved: The edge finishes linking within a few seconds: its page shows the connection as linked.
link.denied: The edge shows that the pairing was denied. To try again, start a new pairing on the edge.
link.codeHint: The edge shows it under Connections after “Add connection”. A link from the edge fills it in; it is valid for 10 minutes.
link.deviceWait: Check a code to see which edge asks to be linked.
link.alreadyResolved: This code was already {{status}}. Start a new pairing on the edge.
link.homeHint: The edge works for this home. Without one, the edge is only registered to you; give it a home later in Fleet.
link.note: An edge that is linked can be unlinked on the edge itself (Connections → unlink); the cloud keeps its data.
link.notFound: No edge is waiting with that code. Check it on the edge's page: a code is valid for 10 minutes, then the edge needs a new one.
link.createFailed: Could not create the home. Check the fields and retry.
link.approveFailed: Approval failed. The code may have expired, or you may not own that home.

homeConfig.title: Configurations
homeConfig.subtitle: The installation of the active home: the live configuration, the versions before it and the planning options. Compare any two.
homeConfig.noHomeId: This home has no permanent id yet. It gets one when an edge linked to it lists its homes; until then it has no configurations or vault.
homeConfig.noVersions: No configuration yet. An edge publishes the installation as it is (a survey) as the first live one.
homeConfig.noOptions: No planning option. An edge creates one, based on the live version.
